p:cNvPr.descr: PART 2: An illustration of the class I aldolase reaction. On the left is a bracketed molecule that begins with C, which bonds up to CH2OPO2 over 3 [negative], left to H over N+, which bonds down to H and bonds left. Below this –B with two red dots to the right has a red arrow pointing from it up to H. A red arrow also points from the bond line between H over N+ and H to the bond line between C and H over N+. C also bonds right to O, which bonds right to H (all in blue). The bond line between C and O has a red arrow from it pointing to H+ in blue. To the right are two red dots to the left of A bonding right. C also bonds down to HOCH. To the very right of this are two red dots with B to the right bonding right. HOCH also bonds down to HC, which bonds right to O, which bonds right to H. HC bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to CH2OPO2 over 3 [negative]. To the right of this are reversible arrows. Another arrow jets off the arrow pointing right to H2) in blue. This is step 2: Rearrangement leads to formation of protonated Schiff base on enzyme; electron delocalization facilitates subsequent steps. To the right of the arrows are protonated Schiff base, where C bonds up to CH2OPO2 over 3[negative] and double bonds left to H over N+, which bonds left to Lys. A red arrow points from the double bond line to the N in H over N+. To the extreme right are two red dots with A to the right and A bonds right. C also bonds down to HOCH, which bonds down to HC. A red arrow points from the bond line between HOCH and HC to the bond line between C and HOCH. HC also bonds right to O, which bonds right to H. A red arrow points from the bond line between O and H back to the bond line between HC and O. To the right are two red dots to the left of B, which bonds right. An arrow points from this back to H. HC also bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to CH2OPO2 over 3[negative]. Just above the last HCOH and to the left is –BH. Below this is the outside frame explained in aldolase without the molecule, and is where the proton exchange with solution restores enzyme.
